title: Unable to Read SD Card
shortDescription: Switch cannot detect or read the inserted microSD card.
fullDescription: Error 2123-1502 indicates the Nintendo Switch cannot read the microSD card. The card may be incompatible (must be UHS-I), corrupted, or seated incorrectly. Reformatting on the console usually resolves it; persistent failure suggests a damaged card or slot.

causes.cause: Dirty or misaligned card slot contacts

symptoms: Console reverts to internal storage only

fixSteps.title: Reseat SD card
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, remove card under kickstand, blow out dust, reinsert firmly until click.

fixSteps.title: Test on PC
fixSteps.instruction: Insert card into a PC reader. Verify files; back up immediately.

fixSteps.title: Format on Switch
fixSteps.instruction: System Settings > System > Formatting Options > Format microSD Card. Reinstall games from eShop.

whenToCallPro: If SD slot itself is damaged.

faq.a: Saves are stored on internal storage, not the SD card.

title: Unable to Connect to Server
shortDescription: Switch cannot reach Nintendo eShop or online services.
fullDescription: Error 2155-8007 appears when the Switch cannot connect to Nintendo's eShop servers. Common causes are router DNS issues, server outages, or strict NAT.

fixSteps.title: Check Nintendo status page
fixSteps.instruction: Visit nintendo.com/status to confirm services are online.

fixSteps.title: Change DNS
fixSteps.instruction: System Settings > Internet > network > Change Settings > DNS Settings > Manual. Primary 8.8.8.8 secondary 8.8.4.4.

fixSteps.title: Restart router
fixSteps.instruction: Power-cycle modem and router for 60 seconds.

faq.a: No, this is a connection error not an account issue.

title: WiFi Connection Timeout
shortDescription: Switch fails to authenticate with WiFi network.
fullDescription: Error 2110-3127 means the Switch could not complete the WiFi handshake. Usually a 2.4GHz/5GHz incompatibility or weak signal.

fixSteps.title: Move closer to router
fixSteps.instruction: Place Switch within 10 feet, line of sight.

fixSteps.title: Switch to 2.4GHz
fixSteps.instruction: Forget current network. Connect to 2.4GHz SSID instead of 5GHz.

fixSteps.title: Change channel
fixSteps.instruction: In router admin, set 2.4GHz to channel 1, 6, or 11.

whenToCallPro: If multiple devices have same issue.

faq.a: Yes, dock LAN adapter gives stable connection.

title: Software Closed Due to Error
shortDescription: A game crashed and the system closed it.
fullDescription: Error 2002-2060 indicates the running software encountered a fatal error and was closed. Often caused by corrupted save data or an outdated game.

fixSteps.title: Update game
fixSteps.instruction: Highlight game, press +, Software Update > Via Internet.

fixSteps.title: Clear cache
fixSteps.instruction: System Settings > System > Formatting Options > Clear Cache (per user).

faq.a: Cloud save users can restore; otherwise saves remain unless deleted.

title: System Memory Damaged
shortDescription: Console reports corruption in system NAND memory.
fullDescription: Error 2168-0002 means system data is corrupt. Sometimes recoverable via initialization without deleting saves, but often requires service.

fixSteps.title: Initialize without deleting saves
fixSteps.instruction: Hold Power+VolUp+VolDown to enter Maintenance Mode. Choose Initialize Console Without Deleting Save Data.

fixSteps.title: Full initialization
fixSteps.instruction: If above fails, full initialize (saves lost unless cloud-backed).

fixSteps.title: Send to Nintendo
fixSteps.instruction: If still failing, request repair at nintendo.com/repair.

whenToCallPro: If initialization fails, send to Nintendo.

faq.a: Sometimes recoverable; if not, Nintendo repair is needed.

title: Dock HDMI Output Failure
shortDescription: Switch fails to output to TV via dock.
fullDescription: Error 2206-0310 relates to HDMI handshake failure. Often caused by USB-C cable wear in the dock or HDCP issues.
symptoms: Switch shows charging but no video

fixSteps.title: Reseat cables
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug and reinsert HDMI and USB-C in dock.

fixSteps.title: Try different HDMI port/cable
fixSteps.instruction: Test another TV port and a known-good HDMI 2.0 cable.

fixSteps.title: Replace dock
fixSteps.instruction: If issue persists, replace with official Nintendo dock.

whenToCallPro: If console damaged from third-party dock.

faq.a: Some have caused damage; stick with Nintendo or reputable brands.

title: Joy-Con Analog Stick Drift
shortDescription: Joy-Con registers movement when stick is centered.
fullDescription: Joy-Con drift is caused by dust in the potentiometer or wear of the contact pads. Nintendo offers free repairs in many regions.

fixSteps.title: Recalibrate stick
fixSteps.instruction: System Settings > Controllers > Calibrate Control Sticks.

fixSteps.title: Compressed air
fixSteps.instruction: Tilt stick, blast compressed air around base.

fixSteps.title: Free Nintendo repair
fixSteps.instruction: Submit request at nintendo.com/repair (free in US/EU).

fixSteps.title: Replace stick module
fixSteps.instruction: Open Joy-Con with tri-wing screwdriver, replace stick module.

faq.a: Yes, Nintendo waives the fee for drift in most regions.

title: The Console is Too Warm
shortDescription: Switch displays overheat warning and throttles.
fullDescription: Switch shuts down or warns when internal temperature exceeds safe limits. Caused by blocked vents, dried thermal paste, or dust buildup.

fixSteps.title: Improve ventilation
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure dock has 4 inches clearance behind and above.

fixSteps.title: Clean vents
fixSteps.instruction: Compressed air through top and bottom vents.

fixSteps.title: Repaste
fixSteps.instruction: Disassemble, clean old paste from APU, apply new thermal compound.

faq.q: Is BotW known to cause this?
faq.a: Demanding games push thermals; ensure ventilation.

title: eShop Purchase Failed
shortDescription: Payment was not completed for an eShop purchase.
fullDescription: Error 2813-0002 occurs when the eShop cannot complete a transaction, usually due to declined card or region mismatch.

fixSteps.title: Verify payment method
fixSteps.instruction: Account > Payment Methods. Update CVV and billing ZIP.

fixSteps.title: Add funds first
fixSteps.instruction: Buy eShop credit, then purchase from balance.

fixSteps.title: Try later
fixSteps.instruction: Retry after 30 minutes if servers were busy.

whenToCallPro: Contact bank if card repeatedly declined.

faq.a: Failed transactions are not finalized; pending holds clear in 3-5 days.

title: Switch Blue Screen Crash
shortDescription: Console freezes on a solid blue screen.
fullDescription: The Switch BSOD indicates a kernel panic, often from corrupt firmware, failing eMMC, or modchip / homebrew issues.

faq.a: Maintenance init preserves saves; full reset does not.

fullDescription: Switch hardware fault. Common indication on Nintendo Switch.
whenToCallPro: If reset/reinstall fail, contact manufacturer support.
